transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Linda Kenyon.
There are new details in the investigation of the mid-air attack aboard a commercial plane from Dubai to Tel Aviv earlier this week.
NPR's Kat Lonsdorf reports the United Arab Emirates, which is leading the probe, has deemed the incident an attempted terrorist attack.
Investigators in the UAE announced that the Fly Dubai co-pilot who carried out the attack mid-flight assaulted the captain of the plane using what's called a crash axe,
a lightweight emergency tool stored in the cockpit to break through panels or jam doors in the event of a crash.
Investigators said the attacker then tried to seize control of the plane's flight mechanisms.
The plane had 174 people on board, many of whom are Israeli.
Israeli officials had already deemed it an attempted terrorist attack.
Emirati investigators have now agreed. Both the pilot and co-pilot are live and being questioned, and the investigation is ongoing.
Israel has said the attacker is from Oman, although that has yet to be confirmed by Emirati, Saudi, or Omani officials.
Kat Lonsdorf, NPR News, Tel Aviv.
President Trump continues a series of rallies to support Republican candidates heading into the midterm elections with a stop in Ohio tonight.
Jerry Kenney from member station WYSO has the story.
Trump is stumping for the incumbent Republican Senate candidate, John Husted, who's in a tight race with former Ohio Senator, Sherrod Brown.
Husted was appointed by Governor Mike DeWine to fill Vice President J.D. Vance's Senate seat in 2025.
The president is sure to tout his economic accomplishments tonight, but with low approval ratings and many Americans still reeling from high gas prices and other economic struggles,
it's unclear if his message will resonate with voters and help carry Husted over the finish line in November.
For NPR News, I'm Jerry Kenney in Yellow Springs.
The architect of Tennessee's lethal injection protocols is stepping down from his position after the second botched execution this year.
Marianna Baca Yau reports from member station WPLN in Nashville.
Frank Strada helped design the state's new execution process after a 2020 review found that Tennessee had not properly inspected the drugs it uses to put people to death.
Strada came to Tennessee from Arizona, where he oversaw three botched executions similar to Wednesdays.
Christa Pike did not die after receiving two full doses of pentobarbital.
Usually, just one dose is considered lethal.
Pike's attorneys say she is unconscious and on a ventilator at an area hospital following Wednesday's botched execution.
For NPR News, I'm Marianna Baca Yau in Nashville.
Celebrated visual artist Theaster Gates is the new owner of the last remaining manufacturer of fine china in the United States, Picard China.
NPR's Chloe Veltman has the story.
Located near Chicago, Picard had, up until now, been run by the Picard family ever since its founding in 1893.
The porcelain company's customers include the White House, U.S. embassies and higher-end retailers.
But the industry has been in decline for decades.
Picard's new owner, Theaster Gates, says he wants to turn things around.
That idea that Picard could be a place bringing artisanal manufacturing back to the fore, that's very exciting.
Gates is a master ceramicist himself.
He's also known for restoring and repurposing defunct buildings and businesses.
The artist says he plans to guide Picard's creative strategy and build a team to manage daily operations.
Chloe Veltman, NPR News.
The Federal Trade Commission has settled with Southern Glazers' wine and spirits over claims it discriminated against some businesses.
The FTC sued the alcohol distributor in December 2024, alleging it favored larger stores like Walmart
when it came to discounts and did not offer those same discounts to smaller retailers.
Under the terms of the settlement, Southern Glazers must compensate smaller retailers if it gives better prices to larger chains,
while an independent monitor will oversee the settlement for a period of six years.
Southern Glazers denies wrongdoing, but also says it is pleased with the settlement.
I'm Linda Kenyon, NPR News in Washington.
You can get free through Amazon Music, or you can also support NPR's vital journalism and get NPR+ at plus.npr.org.
That's plus.npr.org.

topics.text: UAE investigators confirm Fly Dubai co-pilot attacked captain with crash axe, deemed attempted terrorist attack
President Trump holds rally in Ohio to support Republican Senate candidate John Husted
Tennessee execution protocol architect Frank Strada steps down after second botched execution this year
Artist Theaster Gates becomes new owner of Picard China, last U.S. fine china manufacturer
FTC settles with Southern Glazers wine distributor over alleged discrimination against smaller retailers
